Meter it — leads are often all black.
32.768 kHz will NOT run this chip.
AMBER = Arduino pin name · BLUE = net / function · Pin 20 AVCC MUST be tied to +5 V.
B — PROGRAMMING: ARDUINO UNO DIP SWAP
1. Board = "Arduino Uno". Upload the sketch to the Uno.
2. Unplug USB. Lever the chip out, alternating ends so the legs stay straight.
3. Fit it to your socket, notch to the same end as the schematic shows.
4. No fuse changes needed — the Uno already runs 16 MHz off an external crystal,
which is exactly what your Y1 provides.
STAR GND — all returns meet here
▸ C5 and C9 within 10 mm of
▸ Y1 and its 22 pF caps hard
SW1 is a hard master switch in
the +12 V line — it kills everything,
so the MCU never sees it.
1. Fit U1 ONLY. Power up, trim output to 5.00 V. Power down.
2. Meter +12 V–GND and +5 V–GND for shorts. Expect > 1 kΩ.
3. Fit U2, Y1, caps, LCD. Power up: 2 s splash, both fans 100 %.
4. Blank screen? Change LCD_ADDRESS to 0x3F, or trim the backpack
5. Pot fully down → fans stop, screen reads STOPPED.
6. Unplug fan B while running → LED B blinks fast within 3 s and
the screen reads !FAN B NO SIGNAL. Replug → clears.
TEST POINTS TP1 +12 V TP2 +5 V TP3 Q1 collector
TP4 tach A TP5 tach B TP6 D9 / pin 15
Also: 2× Corsair 120 mm 4-pin PWM fan, F1 2 A slow-blow fuse + holder, SW1 illuminated car-type rocker, 12 V 2 A PSU, carbon pad, mesh pre-filter, USB-A socket + 1.1 A PTC (sheet 3).
